drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Counsel — attached is Seller’s final movement for this round. We have accepted the core of your financial-statement point: the rep is now unqualified by materiality, tied to GAAP consistently applied, and schedule exceptions must be specific rather than a blanket carveout. On indemnity, Seller can move to 18-month survival, a true deductible basket at 0.75% of Purchase Price, and a 15% cap, with customary exclusions for fraud, intentional breach, covenants, and fundamental representations. We have also tightened the effect of disclosure so that only specifically identified exceptions qualify the applicable representation to the extent fairly disclosed. We think this should put the document in a place the parties can sign.

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. The Seller shall have no liability for any Losses unless and until aggregate indemnifiable Losses exceed an amount equal to 0.75% of the Purchase Price, in which event the Seller shall be liable only for Losses in excess of such amount. The Seller's aggregate liability for indemnifiable Losses shall not exceed 15% of the Purchase Price. The basket, cap, and survival limitations in this Section 4 shall not apply to claims arising from fraud, intentional breach, breach of covenants, or breach of fundamental representations. A matter disclosed in the Disclosure Schedule shall limit indemnity only to the extent such matter is specifically identified with reasonable particularity and the relevance of such disclosure to the applicable representation or warranty is reasonably apparent on its face.
